title: Counting on from the bigger number
examples: How do I add 8 and 3 without counting from one?
Why start with the bigger number?

explain.say: Imagine adding eight and three. Do you start at one and count all the way up? That takes ages! Here is a quicker way: counting on. Look at the number line on the board.

draw.text: Counting on from the bigger number

explain.say: Put eight in your head. Tap your head and say eight! You already know it is there, so there is no need to count up to it. Can you find eight on the line?
Now hop on three times: nine, ten, eleven. Hold up one finger for each hop. Three hops, and you land on eleven. So eight and three make eleven!
Tip: start with the bigger number. For two and nine, start at nine, not two. Then just two hops: ten, eleven. Much quicker! Can you see why?
Try fourteen and four. Start at fourteen, then hop: fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen. Fantastic! Challenge: what is twenty and three? Start at twenty!

faq.a: Counting on means starting at one number and counting forward from it, instead of starting from one. For eight and three, start at eight and say nine, ten, eleven.

faq.q: Why start with the bigger number?
faq.a: Fewer hops! For two and nine, starting at nine means only two hops, not nine.
asks: Which number do I start with?

faq.q: How do I keep track of my hops?
faq.a: Hold up one finger for each hop, or tap the table. Stop when your fingers show the number you are adding.
asks: How do I count my hops?

faq.q: Do I say the first number again?
faq.a: No. Keep the first number in your head, then start counting with the next number. For eight and three, say nine, ten, eleven.
A number line is a line with numbers in order, like a ruler. You can hop along it to add or take away.
asks: Tell me about the number line

facts: Adding numbers in any order gives the same answer, so 2 + 9 and 9 + 2 both make 11.

quiz.why: Start at nine and hop two: ten, eleven.

wrong.1: Ten is only one hop from nine. You need two hops.
wrong.2: Twelve is three hops from nine. You need two.

quiz.say: To add 3 and 10, where is the quickest place to start?
quiz.why: Start at the bigger number, ten, and hop three times.

wrong.1: Starting at three means ten hops. Starting at ten is quicker.
wrong.2: Starting at one means counting everything. Count on from ten instead.
